title: Keep compaction ahead of incoming writes
description: Match a workload to a compaction strategy, then test whether background capacity and free disk can sustain it without an ever-growing backlog.

workloads.label: Write-heavy event store
workloads.detail: High ingest, mostly point reads, and frequent new keys favor low rewrite work.

workloads.label: Mixed key-value service
workloads.detail: Point reads, updates, and range scans all matter, so predictable read amplification is valuable.

workloads.label: Range-heavy catalog
workloads.detail: Ordered scans are common and overwritten keys should converge into a small set of non-overlapping runs.

strategies.label: Size-tiered
strategies.detail: Merge similarly sized runs in batches. This limits rewrite work but leaves more overlapping runs for reads.

strategies.label: Leveled
strategies.detail: Keep most levels non-overlapping. Reads inspect fewer runs, while bytes may be rewritten repeatedly as levels grow.
